fields.title: 2. Event ② — Qualcomm's Starlink Mobile Terrestrial Network Contract: Announcement vs. Filing
fields.md:
| Date (US) | Fact | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| **2026-11-04 (Wed)** | **Qualcomm press release** "SpaceX Selects Qualcomm to Accelerate Starlink Mobile's Nationwide 5G Network" — this round's tool **rendered only the title** (body not read); the body was confirmed through trade-press reprints: SpaceX adopts the Dragonwing **QRU100** (radio unit) and **QDU100** (distributed unit) platforms plus commercial-grade **Layer 1** software · **64T64R Massive MIMO** · nationwide deployment **starting 2027**, **tens of thousands of sites** over the multi-year contract · phase 1 is terrestrial 5G only, later multi-band and 'AI-native 6G' based · **amount undisclosed**. Qualcomm EVP **Durga Malladi**: "Building a nationwide network demands high performance and power efficiency at every site". **SpaceX-side quote — Starlink SVP Michael Nicolls**: "Starlink is building the first fully-integrated nationwide satellite and terrestrial network" | ② [Qualcomm press release (title only verified)](https://www.qualcomm.com/news/releases/2026/11/spacex-selects-qualcomm-to-accelerate-starlink-mobile-s-nationwi) · ⑥ [FoneArena 11/04 (press release reprint)](https://www.fonearena.com/blog/496422/spacex-qualcomm-dragonwing-starlink-mobile-terrestrial-5g-network.html) · [Converge Digest 11/04](https://convergedigest.com/spacex-qualcomm-dragonwing-starlink-mobile-5g/) |
| 2026-11-04 | **Reuters 08:34 ET**: Qualcomm called it the "biggest 5G deal yet" — multi-year supply of radio equipment, baseband and software, **tens of thousands of macro cell sites** from 2027, amount undisclosed. An expansion of the infrastructure business, competing with Marvell, Broadcom and Intel | ⑤ [Reuters (Investing.com reprint)](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/qualcomm-signs-major-5g-infrastructure-deal-with-spacex-for-starlink-mobile-network-4999443) |
| 2026-11-04 | **CNBC 08:30 ET**: the terrestrial network will "complement Starlink's satellite capabilities", construction starts next year, tower partners and number of towers needed undisclosed · Starlink is 36% of 3Q revenue and 85% of operating profit · agreement in October on acquiring nationwide 800MHz spectrum | ⑤ [CNBC 11/04](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/spacex-strikes-deal-with-qualcomm-for-mobile-network-infrastructure.html) |
| 2026-11-04 | **Malladi (Converge Digest)**: Massive MIMO is usually used above 3.5GHz, but this time 64T64R is placed on **2GHz (SpaceX mid-band = EchoStar AWS-4/H)** · the sites are macro towers (not small cells) · **SpaceX builds the RU and DU hardware itself and develops the L2/L3 software on top of the Qualcomm PHY, through to the core network** · 2GHz = capacity layer, 800MHz = coverage layer | ⑥ [Converge Digest 11/04](https://convergedigest.com/spacex-qualcomm-dragonwing-starlink-mobile-5g/) · [Notebookcheck 11/04](https://www.notebookcheck.net/SpaceX-recruits-Qualcomm-to-challenge-America-s-biggest-mobile-carriers.1442194.0.html) (Grain 800MHz: **up to 14MHz paired**, subject to regulatory approval) |
| 2026-11-04 | StockTwits (Yahoo reprint): on the 3Q call, Shotwell said 'service launch in early 2028' and Musk said 'we will build a terrestrial network' (candidate table) · full transfer of EchoStar licenses scheduled for 2027-11 · SPCX −4% intraday (roughly two-month low) | ⑥ [StockTwits (Yahoo) 11/04 07:07 PT](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/qualcomm-spacex-team-build-starlink-150721582.html) |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K or IR press release**. **Qualcomm's 8-K (11/4) covers earnings (Items 2.02·9.01)**, and a full-text search of the 10-K filed the same day returned 0 hits for 'SpaceX' — Qualcomm also did not treat this contract as a disclosure event | ① [SpaceX EDGAR](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json) · [Qualcomm EDGAR 8-K list](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000804328&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=5) · [EDGAR full-text search (Qualcomm, 11/1~11/6, 'SpaceX')](https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22SpaceX%22&ciks=0000804328&dateRange=custom&startdt=2026-11-01&enddt=2026-11-06), accessed 2026-11-05 |

**EchoStar filing from the same week (T9 input — primary text, not press coverage)**: EchoStar **3Q26 10-Q (11/3)** — wireless (Boost) segment revenue **$905,152 thousand** (3Q25 $936,571 thousand; −2.6% vs. 2Q26 $929.0M; formula: 905.2 ÷ 929.0 − 1) · wireless OIBDA $109,036 thousand (3Q25 −$138,858 thousand) · 'SpaceX Transactions — Restricted Licenses' carrying value **$8,667,276 thousand** (9/30) · 'the timing and closing of the SpaceX Transactions are not certain' (risk factors) · following deconsolidation of subsidiaries, the Pay-TV and broadband segments are unconsolidated from 3Q. Subscribers are not in XBRL — press reports: **182,000 net loss, about 7.19 million (10-Q 7.193M)**, ARPU $39.10, consensus −74,000. The 11/3 8-K (Item 5.07) reports the 10/30 shareholder meeting results (director elections, KPMG, compensation) and is unrelated to SpaceX. **The EchoStar 10-Q also has no mention of Boost discussions or Qualcomm** (scope read: cover, financial statements, risk factors, R16, R70, R73, R81) (Sources: ① [EchoStar 10-Q R73](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000110465926121675/R73.htm) · [R70](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000110465926121675/R70.htm) · [R16](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000110465926121675/R16.htm) · [10-Q body](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000110465926121675/sats-20260930x10q.htm) · [8-K 11/03](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1415404/000141540426000057/sats-20261030x8k.htm) · ⑥ [Broadband Breakfast 11/03](https://broadbandbreakfast.com/echostar-wireless-losses-worse-than-expected/) · `state.triggers_next_12m[T9].note` (2Q26 $929.0M)).

**Confirmed as fact (official announcement by the counterparty + two tier-1 reports)**: ① Qualcomm announced a multi-year supply contract on 11/4, and a SpaceX executive is quoted in that material ② the scope is chips and L1 software for terrestrial 5G base stations, construction starting 2027, tens of thousands of sites ③ amount, tower partners, number of sites and commercial launch date undisclosed ④ no SpaceX filing of its own. **Unconfirmed**: contract amount and CAPEX size (in no source text — no estimation) · number of sites · conditions for starting 2GHz operation (DA 26-1078 condition 3: after EchoStar phase 2 closes, around 2027-11-30 — `state.triggers_next_12m[T8]`) · relationship to the Boost discussions (Source: table above).

### 2-1. What the Two Events Touch

| Item | Content | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| T5 · $40 billion GPU master financial lease | Syndication talks are read as the start of the 'pricing' stage described in the 8-K → the signing 8-K (Item 1.01, fixed rate) is consistent with the 'closing before year-end' schedule. The expectation was not wrong. Check point 2027-01-07 maintained, monthly check point 12/01 added. **The monitor's link to T1 was wrong** — it appears to stem from the overlapping names 'AI' and '4Q', but the cause lies with the measurement layer | Partially confirmed maintained · syndication stage added to check |
| D-2027-1 (additional financing ≤ $50 billion AND no equity raise) | The lessor-side loan of $8.3 billion plus bonds (reported) fall under 'financing of an off-balance-sheet vehicle for which the company bears payment obligations' in `definitions.additional_financing` — already counted within the $40 billion, with the booking year 2027 (commencement). The $7 billion prepayment (reported) is not financing but a **cash outflow for SpaceX** — if true, it is an input to liquidity and cash burn rate (Axis D dissection), not a milestone. No equity raise element (no change) | Undetermined maintained · report recorded in progress_reason |
| Proposed new rule ② (fixed rate above 8%) | The rate is not in the reports either — deliberation remains on hold | Not triggered |
| Proposed new rule ③ (off-balance-sheet → consolidated debt) | A Reuters reprint (rallies.ai) again described it as an 'off-balance-sheet structure' — the 8-K does not state accounting treatment. Verdict stays with the first 10-Q after commencement | Not triggered |
| A-2028-1 (30 million subscribers · separately disclosed D2C revenue of $3 billion) | The definition of Starlink Mobile has widened from 'satellite D2C' to 'satellite + own terrestrial network' (Qualcomm announcement + Nicolls quote). The milestone wording 'separately disclosed D2C revenue' has no definition of **whether it includes terrestrial subscriber revenue** — the monthly round (12/01) will decide. Not a current verdict input (no revenue disclosure) | Progress maintained · definition task registered |
| T9 · Boost/EchoStar terrestrial network | There are now two paths — ⓐ **acquisition/MVNO (Boost)**: reported stage, not mentioned in the EchoStar 10-Q, Boost subscribers net −182,000 (reported) ⓑ **own build (Qualcomm)**: official announcement by the counterparty. No source text says whether ⓑ replaces or complements ⓐ → T9 is widened to 'terrestrial network — transaction (ⓐ) + own build (ⓑ)', with ⑦ equipment/tower contract disclosures and ⑧ 10-K purchase commitment notes added to check | On hold maintained · scope expanded |
| Scenarios (Connectivity) | The Connectivity assumptions (subscribers, ARPU) of the 3 scenarios **have no terrestrial CAPEX or operating cost item**. Since the amount is nowhere available, the numbers are left untouched — the monthly round will decide 'which cell to put terrestrial CAPEX in once disclosed' | No change · design task registered |
| Probability rules R1~R6 | Conditions do not include syndication or terrestrial network | Not triggered |
| E-2027-4 · Axis E | Unrelated | No change |

(Sources: `state.definitions.additional_financing` · `state.milestones[A-2028-1·D-2027-1]` · `state.triggers_next_12m[T5·T9]` · tables in Sections 1–2)
